newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Soldiers and Colombian coca growers clash.
newsitem.headline: Soldiers and Colombian coca growers clash.

text.p: Peasant farmers clashed with soldiers, injuring 20 with stones and firebombs, on Monday in the latest violence stemming from a 40-day-old protest in southern Caqueta province, authorities said.

Military sources said demonstrators protesting U.S.-backed plans to eradicate coca leaf plantations in the region hurled stones and Molotov cocktails at security forces near the town of Morelia after they found their way across a bridge blocked.
More than 20 soldiers suffered slight injuries, the sources said. Troops responded by firing teargas and four peasant leaders were arrested, they added.

Negotiations to end the uprising were suspended in the province's main city, Florencia, on Friday. They had been due to restart on Monday in the capital Bogota but were delayed after peasant representatives failed to arrive in time for midday talks with Interior Minister Horacio Serpa.

Thousands of protesters have been camped out in Morelia for the past month after their way to Florencia was barred. Similar protests in the neighboring province of Putumayo, which began in July, were resolved but demonstrations in Guaviare are continuing and at least 12 demonstrators have been killed.

Peasant farmers say growing coca leaf, which is processed to produce cocaine, is the only viable way for them to make a living. They argue that government measures to promote crop substitution are insufficient.
Colombia has promised the United States that it will eradicate 44,500 acres (18,000 hectares) of coca leaf this year -- Latin America's most ambitious fumigation program.

Defense chiefs have accused Colombia's oldest and largest guerrilla group, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), of inciting the peasant uprising. FARC is said by the military to specialize in protecting clandestine cocaine laboratories and drug routes.
